data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Practise reporting questions, requests, instructions and commands with appropriate word order and tense changes.
learningPoints: Use statement word order in reported questions.
Use if or whether for reported yes/no questions.
Use ask/tell + object + to-infinitive for requests and commands.
Use not to for negative commands.
Distinguish reporting verbs according to meaning and structure.

sections.explain: Reported questions use statement word order after the question word.

words.word: She asked me where I lived.
She asked me where did I live.
She asked me where I did lived.

sections.explain: Use IF or WHETHER for reported yes/no questions.

words.word: He asked if I was ready.
He asked was I ready.
He asked if was I ready.

sections.explain: A present tense can shift back when the question is reported later.

words.word: 'What are you doing?' → She asked what I was doing.
'What are you doing?' → She asked what was I doing.
'What are you doing?' → She asked what I am do.

sections.explain: Use ASK + object + TO + verb for a reported request.

words.word: She asked me to close the window.
She asked that I close the window to.
She asked me closing the window.

sections.explain: Use TELL + object + TO + verb for a reported command or instruction.

words.word: The officer told us to wait outside.
The officer told to us wait outside.
The officer told us waiting outside.

sections.explain: Use TELL/ASK + object + NOT TO + verb.

words.word: He told me not to touch the switch.
He told me to not touching the switch.
He told not me to touch the switch.

sections.explain: WHETHER can be used instead of IF in reported yes/no questions.

words.word: They asked whether we had finished.
They asked whether had we finished.
They asked did we have finished.

sections.explain: Modals can backshift or remain depending on meaning; word order still becomes statement order.

words.word: He asked whether I could help him.
He asked whether could I help him.
He asked did I could help him.

sections.summary: Using the correct reporting verb pattern.
sections.explain: REQUEST can be reported with ASK; a direct instruction commonly uses TELL.

words.word: The teacher told the students to hand in their work.
The teacher said the students to hand in their work.
The teacher told that the students hand in their work.

sections.explain: Keep the question word but use statement word order.

words.word: I asked her why she had left early.
I asked her why had she left early.
I asked her why did she had left early.
